discovery: Discovery of Bose-Einstein condensation of excitons in quantum Hall bilayers

nominees.name: Allan H. MacDonald
nominees.affiliation: University of Texas at Austin, USA

subfield: Condensed matter physics / mesoscopic and low-dimensional electron systems
motivation: In closely spaced GaAs double quantum wells at total filling factor one, electrons in one layer pair with holes in the other to form an interlayer exciton condensate. Eisenstein and co-workers showed this with a series of decisive transport experiments: a giant zero-bias tunneling peak like the Josephson effect, vanishing Hall resistance under counterflow, quantized Hall drag, and dissipationless exciton transport in Corbino geometry. MacDonald's theory predicted the spontaneous interlayer phase coherence and the superfluid response that these experiments test. Pfeiffer's ultra-high-mobility heterostructures, with independently contacted layers, made the measurements possible. Together their work gave the first unambiguous realization of exciton Bose-Einstein condensation in a solid, a goal pursued for half a century. It set the reference point for electron-hole bilayers, Coulomb drag and the excitonic condensates now being explored in graphene and transition-metal dichalcogenide heterostructures. It is a model of many-body physics built on sample engineering and careful measurement.
